answer: Latency triangulation pins each agent to a real place. Validators scattered around the globe ping every identity and time the replies, so physics reveals roughly where it runs. If a hundred agents all answer from the same spot, like boats moored at one reef, they are grouped and share a single reward. To fake distinct identities an attacker must rent servers in many separate regions, each like a lantern lit on its own hill, and keep them online at their zenith of uptime. That is a real hosting bill per fake.
